# Legacy factory compatibility (Java migration)

Scenario v2 does not use factories. Author new integrations with ordinary code inside `Scenario.define` as described in `implement.md` and `scenarios.md`.

This page exists only for projects migrating older customer code that already calls `FactoryUtil.defineFactory`. The helper is not registered with the handler, is not discoverable, and is never invoked by the v2 protocol. Do not introduce it in a new v2 integration.

## Temporary use during migration

Existing helper calls may remain temporarily while their creation and cleanup behavior moves into scenario-owned functions. New v2 code should call those functions directly from `up` and `down`.

## The shape

`FactoryUtil.defineFactory(...)` builds a `FactoryDefinition`. It has three overloads:

| Signature | Use when |
|-----------|----------|
| `defineFactory(create, inputClass)` | Create only, no teardown. |
| `defineFactory(create, inputClass, teardown)` | Create plus teardown. |
| `defineFactory(create, inputClass, teardown, refClass)` | Also convert the stored record to a typed `refClass` before teardown. |

`create` must not be null and `inputClass` must not be null - the SDK throws `IllegalArgumentException` at construction otherwise.

```java
// src/main/java/com/example/autonoma/UserFactory.java
import ai.autonoma.sdk.FactoryUtil;
import ai.autonoma.sdk.types.FactoryDefinition;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.Map;

public static FactoryDefinition userFactory(UserService service) {
  return FactoryUtil.defineFactory(
      (data, ctx) -> {                          // create
        Input input = (Input) data;
        User user = service.create(input.email);
        Map<String, Object> record = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        record.put("id", user.getId());
        record.put("email", user.getEmail());
        return record;
      },
      Input.class,                              // inputClass (required)
      (record, ctx) -> {                        // teardown (optional)
        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
        Map<String, Object> r = (Map<String, Object>) record;
        service.delete((String) r.get("id"));
      });
}

public static class Input {
  public String email;
}
```

`ctx` is a `FactoryContext` record with `refs()`, `scenarioName()`, and `testRunId()`. You call `create`/`teardown` yourself from inside your scenario's `up`/`down`; the SDK never invokes them.

## Using it from a scenario

Wire a factory's output into your scenario's `teardown` so `down` can undo it:

```java
Scenario.define(
    "with-user",
    "One user created through the user factory",
    ctx -> {
      FactoryContext fctx = new FactoryContext(Map.of(), "with-user", ctx.testRunId());
      Map<String, Object> user = userFactory(userService).create().create(
          Map.of("email", UniqueUtil.uniqueEmail(ctx.testRunId(), null, null)), fctx);
      return ScenarioUpResult.builder()
          .teardown(Map.of("userId", user.get("id")))
          .build();
    },
    ctx -> userService.delete((String) ctx.teardown().get("userId")));
```

Because the factory idiom is entirely inside your own code, use it only if it reads more clearly than plain service calls. Everything the platform sees is still just what `up` returns and what `down` tears down.
